question: Who among the following was the captain of the Indian cricket team in the 1983 World Cup?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kapil Dev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kapil Dev was the captain of the Indian cricket team during the 1983 Cricket World Cup.
 
• Under his leadership, India won its first-ever Cricket World Cup on June 25, 1983.
 
• India defeated the West Indies in the final, which was held at Lord's Cricket Ground in London.
 
• Kapil Dev's all-round performance, including a match-winning 175 not out against Zimbabwe, was instrumental in India's success in the tournament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1983 Cricket World Cup:**

 
 
• The 1983 Cricket World Cup was the third edition of the Cricket World Cup, held from June 9 to June 25, 1983, in England.
 
• Eight countries participated in the tournament: India, West Indies, Australia, England, Pakistan, New Zealand, Sri Lanka, and Zimbabwe.
 
• The format of the tournament was a round-robin group stage followed by knockout semi-finals and a final.
 
• India's victory in the 1983 World Cup is considered one of the greatest achievements in Indian cricket history.
 
 
 
• **Kapil Dev:**
 
 
• Kapil Dev Ramlal Nikhanj, commonly known as Kapil Dev, is a former Indian cricketer and captain.
 
• He was a fast bowler and a hard-hitting middle-order batsman.
 
• He is regarded as one of the greatest all-rounders in the history of cricket.
 
• Kapil Dev was inducted into the ICC Cricket Hall of Fame in 2010.
 
 
 
• **Lord's Cricket Ground:**
 
 
• Lord's Cricket Ground, commonly known as Lord's, is a cricket venue in St John's Wood, London.
 
• It is widely referred to as the "Home of Cricket" and is the headquarters of the Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC).
 
• Lord's has hosted numerous historic cricket matches, including World Cup finals.
 
• The ground is known for its iconic pavilion and the distinctive slope across the field.
